quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Say 'book' with relaxed lips. If you tighten them into a small circle it becomes 'boo-k'.
quests.explanation: Lips are only slightly rounded and the vowel is over before the /k/ arrives. Tighten the lips into a circle and it turns into 'boo-k'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʊ/ is lax with loosely rounded lips and a tongue pulled slightly forward; /uː/ is tense, high and back with tightly rounded, protruded lips.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Push your lips forward into a tight circle and hold the vowel. Feel the tension.
quests.explanation: Final -ue after /l/ spells a long, tightly rounded vowel. The lips protrude and stay there until the word ends.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Push the lips into a small circle for /uː/. For /ʊ/ the rounding is slack and the tongue sits lower and further forward.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The vowel set takes its name from this very word. Say it with loose lips.
quests.explanation: This is the word the vowel set is named after: short, gently rounded, no tense pull.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both vowels are rounded, so rounding alone will not separate them: /uː/ is purer and longer, /ʊ/ brief and a little more open.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Hold the vowel in 'soup' and push the lips far forward. A short loose vowel would sound wrong.
quests.explanation: Ou spells the long vowel here, as it does in 'group'. High tongue, strongly rounded lips.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The quality gap is larger than the length gap. /ʊ/ is not simply a shortened /uː/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: 'Put' rhymes with 'foot', not with 'cut'. Round the lips only slightly.
quests.explanation: It looks like 'but' and sounds like 'foot'. This is one of the few u spellings of the short rounded vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In a mirror, /uː/ shows a tight forward pout and /ʊ/ a gentle, relaxed circle.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The oo is long here. Imagine blowing out a candle: lips pushed forward.
quests.explanation: Dark /l/ tends to blur the contrast, so keep the lips forward and the vowel long to protect it.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Short oo words (book, good, foot) take /ʊ/, long ones (food, moon) take /uː/. No spelling rule separates them, so group them by sound.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Double o can be long or short. Here the vowel is short and the lips barely round.
quests.explanation: Double o cannot tell you which vowel you need. Here it is short and loose, even though 'food' looks identical.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /uː/ is the highest, furthest-back vowel; /ʊ/ is slightly lower and more central, so the tongue relaxes forward.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Same two letters as in 'good', but the lips push forward and the vowel is held.
quests.explanation: The lips protrude and the vowel is held. 'Moon' and 'good' share oo but not the vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Before dark /l/ the contrast gets muddy ('pull' versus 'pool'), so use lip protrusion and length together.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Think of 'bull', not 'cool'. Light rounding, then a dark /l/.
quests.explanation: Oo is short again. By sound, 'wool' pairs with 'pull', not with 'cool'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are rounded, so the extra cue is tension: /uː/ feels tight, /ʊ/ feels slack.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The final -ue is silent. What is left is a held, rounded vowel.
quests.explanation: Final -ue after r spells a long rounded vowel, a silent-e style spelling.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Don't over-lengthen /ʊ/: a held, pouting vowel in 'book' sounds foreign.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Silent l and a confusing ou. It rhymes with 'good', not with 'mood'.
quests.explanation: Ou plus a silent l hides a short lax vowel. 'Could' and 'should' follow the same pattern.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʊ/ is lax with loosely rounded lips and a tongue pulled slightly forward; /uː/ is tense, high and back with tightly rounded, protruded lips.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Here ui spells the sound. Push the lips forward after /dʒ/ and hold.
quests.explanation: Ui spells the long vowel in 'juice', 'fruit' and 'suit', and it stays long even before /s/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Push the lips into a small circle for /uː/. For /ʊ/ the rounding is slack and the tongue sits lower and further forward.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Think of 'bull': same vowel, short and loose, then a dark /l/.
quests.explanation: Short and loose-lipped, easily confused with 'pool', which would need tense, protruded lips.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both vowels are rounded, so rounding alone will not separate them: /uː/ is purer and longer, /ʊ/ brief and a little more open.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Seven letters, one vowel sound at the end, ending the same way as 'blue'.
quests.explanation: Ough collapses to a long rounded vowel here. It has many pronunciations, so learn it word by word.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The quality gap is larger than the length gap. /ʊ/ is not simply a shortened /uː/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Back to the first contrast. 'Mix' is short and loose, with no smile.
quests.explanation: A short vowel clipped by the /ks/ cluster. Stretch it into 'meeks' and you have changed the word.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Check the corners of the mouth: they pull back for /iː/ but stay roughly neutral for /ɪ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The first vowel is not the 'oo' of 'woo'. Keep the lips loose and the vowel quick.
quests.explanation: Stress is on wo-, which holds the short rounded vowel and nothing like the o of 'who'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In a mirror, /uː/ shows a tight forward pout and /ʊ/ a gentle, relaxed circle.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Listen right after the /stj/ cluster: is the vowel rounded and held?
quests.explanation: A /j/ glide leads into the long rounded vowel, giving 'styoo-dent'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Short oo words (book, good, foot) take /ʊ/, long ones (food, moon) take /uː/. No spelling rule separates them, so group them by sound.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Smile and hold. Three consonants come first, but the vowel is long and tense.
quests.explanation: After three consonants the vowel arrives tense and sustained: spread lips, high tongue.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Weak -ing, -ish and -ic endings carry /ɪ/ and are never lengthened. Save the long, tense vowel for stressed syllables.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Compare 'fool' and 'full'. One gets a pushed-forward circle, the other loose lips.
quests.explanation: Short and slack. A protruded, held vowel would give 'fool'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /uː/ is the highest, furthest-back vowel; /ʊ/ is slightly lower and more central, so the tongue relaxes forward.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Another ui spelling: lips round, vowel held.
quests.explanation: Long and rounded in RP. A slight /j/ before it ('syoot') is acceptable but not required.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Before dark /l/ the contrast gets muddy ('pull' versus 'pool'), so use lip protrusion and length together.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The nasal /ŋk/ ending follows a short vowel. Don't smile.
quests.explanation: Short and lax before /ŋk/. Smiling here would drag it towards a tense vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spelling is mixed: ee and ea usually spell /iː/, i and y spell /ɪ/ in most words, with exceptions such as 'machine'.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: A u that sounds nothing like 'cube'. The first syllable is stressed and short.
quests.explanation: A rare u spelling for the short rounded vowel, after /ʃ/. Trust the sound.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are rounded, so the extra cue is tension: /uː/ feels tight, /ʊ/ feels slack.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: A /j/ glide, 'kəm-pyoo-', leads into a vowel that needs protruded lips and some length.
quests.explanation: A /j/ glide leads into the long rounded vowel in the stressed second syllable. The other syllables are weak.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Don't over-lengthen /ʊ/: a held, pouting vowel in 'book' sounds foreign.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Hold the vowel with spread lips. The /tʃ/ and /p/ simply frame it.
quests.explanation: Tense, high, held, with spread lips. 'Chip' would be short and loose.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Try whispering: even without voice the difference in tongue height is audible, which shows that quality, not just length, carries the contrast.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Short vowel, loose lips, tongue slightly forward. It ends in /ʃ/.
quests.explanation: A short vowel with no lip protrusion at all, whatever the meaning of the word suggests.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʊ/ is lax with loosely rounded lips and a tongue pulled slightly forward; /uː/ is tense, high and back with tightly rounded, protruded lips.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Think of 'root'. The ou spelling hides a long, rounded vowel.
quests.explanation: In standard British pronunciation the vowel is long and rounded, as in 'root'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Push the lips into a small circle for /uː/. For /ʊ/ the rounding is slack and the tongue sits lower and further forward.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Say 'rivver' with no smile: the vowel is quick and the lips stay neutral.
quests.explanation: Short and loose in the stressed first syllable, and the -er ending is weak.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A voiceless consonant after the vowel shortens both. If duration seems to vanish, rely on the tense quality of /iː/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The ending -hood is the key. It sounds like 'good', not 'mood'.
quests.explanation: The ending -hood has the same short vowel as 'good'. A long word does not need a long vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both vowels are rounded, so rounding alone will not separate them: /uː/ is purer and longer, /ʊ/ brief and a little more open.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The final oo is spelled like the one in 'good' but sounds like the one in 'noon'. Push the lips forward and hold.
quests.explanation: The stress lands on -noon, which holds the long rounded vowel. The first syllable has a different vowel that is not part of this contrast.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The quality gap is larger than the length gap. /ʊ/ is not simply a shortened /uː/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Two i's, both short. Listen for them rather than for a smile.
quests.explanation: Two short vowels in a row: a weak one, then a stressed one. Neither stretches into the long vowel despite the crowded spelling.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɪ/ is lower and more central than /iː/ on the chart, so the tongue shifts slightly down and back.
